verdict_rule: 0 blockers -> READY TO MERGE; 1-3 -> NEEDS CHANGES; 4+ -> MAJOR REWORK NEEDED

findings.title: Shape mutation leg is vacuous against the actual draw path: reverting draw_tie_mark to a solid ring passes CI
findings.detail: The test pins only the tie_dash_on predicate and constants. Replacing draw_tie_mark's dashed loop with the old solid DrawCircleLinesV loop (leaving tie_dash_on intact) fails no test, so the guarded shape can be deleted silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the draw path itself (e.g. count drawn segments via a pure segment-enumeration proc that draw_tie_mark consumes), so removing the dash modulation from draw_tie_mark breaks the count assertion.
findings.verification_note: Read-verified: palette_polish_test.odin:167-188 pins only constants + the tie_dash_on predicate; repo grep shows no test consumes draw_tie_mark (only assist.odin:401 call + :492 def). Empirically mutation-probed: deleting the dash guard at assist.odin:507-509 (solid ring) -> 'odin test app/render' 83/83 PASS. The PR's own mutation leg mutated tie_dash_on itself, not the draw path.

findings.title: New route_tie violet is only 14.0 deg from router_tier_high (below the 15 deg node-signal canon); both are node-centered rings on routers
findings.detail: The PR claims ">= 62 deg from every tier" but only checked pipe tiers. Router tier rings are also node rings, drawn on routers — exactly where ECMP split nodes are. Tritan-sim distance 21.9 fails the project's own 48 signal threshold.
findings.recommended_fix: Add p.router_tier_basic/mid/high to the tiers array in the hue test; if it then fails (it will), shift route_tie hue (e.g. toward blue/magenta) to clear 15 deg from router_tier_high.
findings.verification_note: Independently recomputed: hue 264.35 vs 250.32 = 14.03 deg < 15 canon minimum; Machado tritan sim-dist 21.9 < T_SIGNAL 48 (deutan 52.8 / protan 94.5 pass); plain RGB 34.9. tiers array at palette_polish_test.odin:158 covers pipe tiers only; draw_tier_ring (view.odin:1694-1706) and draw_tie_mark are both node-centered rings; PR body line 17 claims '>= 62 deg from every tier' listing pipe tiers only.

findings.title: Shape pin tests tie_dash_on in isolation, not its use inside draw_tie_mark — deleting the call site renders a solid ring with tests green
findings.detail: The dashed-ring test only evaluates tie_dash_on(0..SEGS) directly; nothing pins that draw_tie_mark's loop actually consults it. Removing the `if !tie_dash_on(i) { continue }` guard yields a solid warning-shaped ring while all tests still pass.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the call-site linkage: e.g. factor the per-segment draw list into a pure proc (segments drawn vs skipped) and assert draw_tie_mark's segment set equals {i : tie_dash_on(i)}, or extract tie_dash_on's use into a testable enumeration the test consumes.
findings.verification_note: Same read-evidence as the acceptance blocker; empirically covered by the mutation probe (guard deleted -> 83/83 tests green).

findings.title: Dashed-ring quad geometry duplicated verbatim from draw_ring_annulus instead of parameterizing it
findings.evidence: assist.odin 504-519: table := SPAWN_RING_TABLE // local copy — a constant can't be indexed by a runtime index ... j := (i + 1) % SPAWN_RING_SEGS ... rl.DrawTriangle(p1o, p1i, p2o, col) rl.DrawTriangle(p2o, p1i, p2i, col); spawn_fx.odin 384-402: draw_ring_annulus :: proc(v: ^View, c: rl.Vector2, r_in, r_out: f32, col: rl.Color) { ... for i in 0 ..< SPAWN_RING_SEGS { j := (i + 1) % SPAWN_RING_SEGS ... rl.DrawTriangle(p1o, p1i, p2o, col) rl.DrawTriangle(p2o, p1i, p2i, col) } }
findings.detail: The segment-quad construction (table lookup, j wrap, CCW winding, two triangles) is copy-pasted from draw_ring_annulus with only a dash predicate added; future winding/geometry fixes must now land in two places.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend draw_ring_annulus with an optional segment predicate (or a draw_ring_annulus_segments proc) and have draw_tie_mark call it with tie_dash_on.
findings.verification_note: Both regions read: assist.odin:504-519 and spawn_fx.odin:388-403 construct the segment quads identically (table lookup, j wrap, CCW winding, two DrawTriangle calls) modulo the dash predicate.

findings.title: Code comment hard-codes '6 dashes' that depends on SPAWN_RING_SEGS = 36
findings.evidence:
+TIE_DASH_SEG :: 3 // consecutive table segments per dash (30 deg at 36 segs)
+TIE_DASH_COUNT :: SPAWN_RING_SEGS / (2 * TIE_DASH_SEG) // = 6 dashes
findings.detail: The '= 6' and '30 deg' annotations silently become false if SPAWN_RING_SEGS changes; the test pins duty cycle and >=4 dashes, not the stated geometry.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the hard-coded '= 6 dashes' / '30 deg' from the comments, or add a compile-time assert tying them to SPAWN_RING_SEGS == 36.
findings.verification_note: Constants located at assist.odin:476-477, evidence text matches verbatim (cited :116-117 is line-number drift). TIE_DASH_COUNT = SPAWN_RING_SEGS/(2*TIE_DASH_SEG); the test pins TIE_DASH_COUNT >= 4 and the 1/2 duty cycle, not the stated count 6 or 30 deg geometry.

findings.title: PR body claims a 225° hue distance, which is impossible on a 360° hue wheel
findings.evidence:
+- **Hue 264°** — a clear family exit, not a nudge: **225°** from
+  `state_congested` (39°, warm-danger family).
findings.detail: Circular hue distance is capped at 180°; 264°−39° wraps to 135°. The stated margin overstates the actual separation almost twofold.
findings.recommended_fix: State the wrapped distance (135°) in the PR body and in any doc repeating this claim.
findings.verification_note: PR body lines 15-16 quote verbatim; recomputed with the repo's hue_degrees: route_tie 264.35 deg vs state_congested 38.97 deg -> circular distance 134.62 deg (unwrapped delta 225.4 deg is what the PR states).

findings.title: draw_tie_mark omits the degenerate-radius/alpha guard its own precedent draw_ring_annulus carries
findings.evidence:
r := s * 0.62
	th := 2.5 * v.scale
	r_in, r_out := r - th * 0.5, r + th * 0.5
--- precedent spawn_fx.odin:385:
	if r_out <= 0 || r_in < 0 || col.a == 0 {
		return
	}
findings.detail: draw_ring_annulus (the copied precedent) early-returns on r_out <= 0, r_in < 0, or col.a == 0; the new inline copy has no such guard, so a zero/negative-scale or transparent route_tie path draws degenerate/inverted triangles unguarded.
findings.recommended_fix: Either call draw_ring_annulus per dash segment or replicate its `if r_out <= 0 || r_in < 0 || col.a == 0 { return }` guard at the top of the segment loop.
findings.verification_note: spawn_fx.odin:385-387 has 'if r_out <= 0 || r_in < 0 || col.a == 0 { return }'; draw_tie_mark (assist.odin:492-520) has no equivalent.

findings.title: Warm-family classifier is weaker than a numeric hue-separation pin for route_tie vs state_congested
findings.evidence:
testing.expect(t, p.state_congested.r > p.state_congested.g && p.state_congested.g > p.state_congested.b,
		"sanity: state_congested must stay in the warm family")
testing.expect(t, !(p.route_tie.r > p.route_tie.g && p.route_tie.g > p.route_tie.b),
		"route_tie must NOT share the warm warning family")
findings.detail: Brief AC3 asks to pin the hue separation between route_tie and state_congested. Only a boolean channel-ordering classifier pins it; a magenta congested (~280 deg) stays within ~16 deg of the violet tie while passing.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit hue_degrees(p.route_tie) vs hue_degrees(p.state_congested) delta >= 90 expectation, mirroring the existing pipe-tier loop.
findings.verification_note: palette_polish_test.odin:152-155 quote verbatim; the only numeric hue pin is vs pipe tiers (:157-163); briefing AC3 asks to pin the hue separation between route_tie and state_congested.
